correctness.rationale: On the event of a reset before h, the terminal temperature depends only on the independent Poisson increments after time zero; conditioning gives C(h)=exp(-rh)Cov(f(A),f(A+h)) with A exponential of rate r. Integrating against the two gamma densities uses the same age A, and the difference r/(r+u+v)-r²/((r+u)(r+v)) gives the claimed strictly positive kernel. Its quotient by v is u/(r+u)² times (1+v/(r+u))^(-1)(1+v/r)^(-1), giving a uniform relative O(v) bound at the edge. The gamma tail dominates all rate moments. Laplace integration of the edge term gives the factor Γ(p+1)/Γ(p)=p; the ratio of first excess-rate moment to mass yields (p+1)/h+O(h^(-2)). The variance under the tilted density proves strict log-convexity and monotonicity of the log decay rate. With probability rh+O(h²) a reset makes the squared temperature increment (T0-f(A))²+O(h); on no reset the square is O(h²) by bounded f'. Stationarity relates the squared increment to 2(C(0)-C(h)), proving the jump formula. Dominated convergence and strict pointwise decrease in c for positive ages give the exact mean-based inversion.
residual_risks: The phrase about independence of the stationary age transform at line 58 is misleading: the exponentials are evaluated at the same age. The displayed calculation correctly uses their joint transform.
Reported finite quadrature is corroboration only; this decision rests on the analytic calculation and does not certify the numerical benchmark or any microscopic model.
